candidate.answerReason: At their separate rates, five hours of combined work would produce \(19/18\) of the wall. The lost \(1/18\) equals \(5\cdot10=50\) bricks, so the full wall contains 900 bricks.

methods.label: Compare five hours of output
methods.explanation:
Compare how much the two bricklayers would produce in the same five-hour period at their individual rates. The first would build \(5/9\) of the wall, and the second would build \(5/10=1/2\). Together, without the reduction, they would build
\[
\frac59+\frac12=\frac{19}{18}
\]
of the wall.

Their actual output was exactly one wall, so the reduction accounts for \(19/18-1=1/18\) of the wall. Losing \(10\) bricks per hour for \(5\) hours means losing \(50\) bricks. Thus \(1/18\) of the wall contains \(50\) bricks, and the whole wall contains
\[
50\div\frac1{18}=50\cdot18=900
\]
bricks.

Indeed, the individual rates would be \(100\) and \(90\) bricks per hour, and their joint rate \(100+90-10=180\) builds \(900\) bricks in five hours. The answer is \(900\), choice C.
methods.levelReason: Uses fractions of a completed job, rate multiplied by time, and recovery of a whole from a known fractional part.

candidate.annotationRationale: The task target is relating work amounts, rates, and elapsed time, covered by cnm_046. This method represents one wall as the whole job and compares fractional outputs. Unlike-denominator addition supports the comparison, and cnm_p184 recovers the full brick count from its one-eighteenth part. A rate system or denominator-clearing equation is not part of the written route.
